**Maintainer ruling (2026-08-17, recorded by PM session `session_01NYgmGheCzM6NrHZN436Cxf`).** The maintainer accepted the decision-inbox report's recommendations in full, verbatim: 「其他接受你的所有建议」. For this card:

**Ruled: Direction 1 — every `@object-ui/plugin-*` ships its own stylesheet.**
- Each plugin package gains the `scripts/build-css.mjs` step + a `"./style.css": "./dist/index.css"` export, built in the **subtraction shape `@object-ui/fields` already uses** (`@reference` the components theme, emit only what components' published sheet does not already carry) — so a published-state consumer imports one extra sheet per installed plugin and the 21 themed utilities (plus the ~140 plain ones) have a source.
- ⛔ Direction 2 (fold plugin classes into components' sheet) rejected — dependency inversion, and every non-plugin consumer pays the bytes. ⛔ Direction 3 (docs-only: teach self-declared `@theme` + scanning `node_modules` dist) rejected — it re-recommends exactly what the #4858 guide correction just retired.
- Follow-through: the quick-start/plugin guides gain the one-line import per plugin; the #4858-corrected "don't scan node_modules" prose stays true (it holds once the sheets exist).
- Scope today: `plugin-grid` + `plugin-kanban` (the two with measured classes); the build step is the pattern any future plugin inherits.

First-touch grading completes: label flipped `needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue` in the same stroke.

## ⛔ First, a correction to this seat's own handling of this card

This card sat undispatched for an entire round on my note *"has a maintainer ruling, but touches ~20 published packages — needs a size call; the skill routes L/XL to cloud, unavailable this session."*

**That premise was wrong, and the answer was on this card the whole time.** The 2026-08-17 ruling ends with:

> **Scope today: `plugin-grid` + `plugin-kanban`** (the two with measured classes); the build step is the pattern any future plugin inherits.

**Two packages.** I read the card's *measurement* — a survey of all 40 `packages/*/package.json` finding no plugin declares the export — and inferred the *scope* from it, without reading the ruling's scope sentence. ⭐ Third instance this round of the same error: **a check was run against the wrong surface.** I had even recorded "has a maintainer ruling (Direction 1)" in my own notes and still never read the line that sized it.

No size call was ever needed. Dispatching at **M**.

## Pre-dispatch gate

**1. Thread read.** The 2026-08-17 maintainer ruling read in full, including the scope line above and both rejections.

**2. Shadow check.** Nothing in flight touches `packages/plugin-grid/` or `packages/plugin-kanban/` — `#6269` is in `packages/types/`. `#6393` (in the merge queue) is `plugin-form`. No hold; merge `origin/main` again before you push.

**3. Precedent verified against the tree** — the ruling names it and it is complete and copyable:
```
packages/fields/package.json      build: tsc && vite build && node scripts/build-css.mjs
                                  exports["./style.css"]: ./dist/index.css
packages/fields/scripts/build-css.mjs        exists
packages/components/scripts/build-css.mjs    exists
packages/fields/src/index.css     carries the @reference subtraction shape, with its
                                  rationale documented in-source (objectui#4059)
```
And the two targets today:
```
packages/plugin-grid/package.json     build: vite build     style export: (none)
packages/plugin-kanban/package.json   build: vite build     style export: (none)
```

## Scope — Direction 1, as ruled

`plugin-grid` and `plugin-kanban` each gain the `scripts/build-css.mjs` step and a `"./style.css": "./dist/index.css"` export, **built in the subtraction shape `@object-ui/fields` already uses**: `@reference` the components theme so this compilation gets its tokens, its class-based `dark` variant and its `tailwindcss-animate` plugin **without emitting a byte of them**, and emit only what components' published sheet does not already carry.

⭐ **Read `packages/fields/src/index.css`'s header comment before you write anything.** It explains *why* the narrow shape works, and that reasoning is the whole design — copying the mechanism without it is how the subtraction silently becomes a duplication.

**Follow-through, also ruled:** the quick-start / plugin guides gain the one-line import per plugin. The #4858-corrected "don't scan `node_modules`" prose **stays true and must stay** — it holds once the sheets exist. ⛔ Do not re-introduce any advice to scan `node_modules` or to hand-declare `@theme`.

## ⛔ Both rejected directions — do not drift into either

- **Direction 2** (fold plugin classes into components' sheet) — **rejected**: dependency inversion, and every non-plugin consumer pays the bytes.
- **Direction 3** (docs-only: teach self-declared `@theme` + scanning `node_modules` dist) — **rejected**: it re-recommends exactly what the #4858 guide correction just retired.

⚠️ Direction 3 is the tempting one because it is cheap. It is ruled out by name.

## Measure, don't inherit

The card's numbers are from `40d3a3318` and are ~4 days old. **Re-derive them on the merged tree**: the 21 themed utilities used by the two plugins and absent from both published sheets, and the ~140 plain ones. Report your counts next to the card's and say where they differ.

⭐ **The 21 are the load-bearing set**, and the card says why: the ~140 plain classes a consumer could in principle generate by scanning `dist`, but the themed ones cannot come from anywhere, because the `@theme` blocks live in unpublished source. If your re-measure finds the themed count is now zero, that is a premise fork — **stop and report**.

## Tests

- Pin that each new sheet **actually contains** the themed utilities that motivated it, and that it does **not** re-emit what `@object-ui/components`' sheet already carries — the subtraction is the point, and a sheet that duplicates the base passes a naive "does it have the class" test.
- ⛔ **Ghost-assertion guard (mandatory):** run each new assertion against unmodified `origin/main`, capture it **failing**, then passing. Both readings in the PR body.
- ⛔ **Degenerate-control guard:** assert a class that components' sheet **does** carry is absent from the plugin sheet. Without that control, "the sheet has classes" proves nothing about subtraction.
- `objectui run`'s temporary app (`packages/cli/src/utils/app-generator.ts:335`) currently restates its own `@theme` token-for-token. If the published sheets make that restatement removable, **report it — do not remove it here.** That is a separate card.

## Ground rules

Worktree-first: `git worktree add ../objectui-4929 -b claude/issue-4929-plugin-published-stylesheets main && cd ../objectui-4929 && pnpm install`. ⛔ Never `git stash` — `refs/stash` lives in the common `.git` dir and is shared across every worktree of this repo; a `pop` silently restores another agent's work and reports success. ⛔ Never touch `content/docs/releases/`. Changeset: `patch`, one entry per package changed. Run the repo's fast checks before pushing — and **build both packages** to confirm the CSS step actually emits. Open the PR as **draft** with `Fixes #4929` and report back — the PM lands it, ⛔ never self-merge.

Size: M. Model: opus.

**ACCEPT — enqueued.** PM session `session_011SfZeFWrhGLHmfq61xbz4q`, `domain:ui` execution seat. 24 ✅ / 3 skipped / 0 ❌ / 0 pending, `clean`. Reviewed against the **tree**, not the report.

## ⭐⭐ Two negative results reported rather than buried — the best thing in this run

**1. A mutation that left the suite GREEN, disclosed as such.** Swapping the narrow `@reference` entry for a plain `@import 'tailwindcss'` did **not** turn anything red. The dev reported it instead of quietly dropping the leg, explained why it is not a ghost (the subtraction removes the duplicated preflight/theme anyway, so the artifact lands at 11.26 kB vs 11.41 kB), and kept the narrow entry for a **different, measured** reason: it makes a `:root` theme block impossible to emit at all, and such a block loaded after the base sheet would override a consumer's own token overrides.

⭐ And it **corrected its own source comments in a second commit**: they had claimed the wide entry would ship ~170 kB of duplication. Its own measurement disproved its own claim, and it changed the claim rather than the measurement.

**2. ⭐ The first mutation matrix was discarded as a blind instrument.** Every leg exited 1 through `--reporter=basic`, which vitest 4 does not have — *"so five legs read as five confirmations while measuring nothing."* Re-run with a **baseline row**, so a non-zero exit means an assertion rather than a broken invocation.

Five false confirmations that all pointed the way the dev wanted. That is precisely the trap a ghost-assertion guard exists for, applied one level up — to the *harness* rather than the assertions — and caught by the dev on its own work.

## The three CI failures, verified fixed the right way

| gate | how it was fixed | verified |
|---|---|---|
| `check:entry-guard` | `isEntrypoint(import.meta.url)` in the per-package wrappers | ✅ and ⛔ **the SHRINK-ONLY baseline was never touched** — `check:check-entry-guard` reports *"48 scripts/ file(s) — no entry guard outside the baseline"* |
| `turbo-build-inputs` | added the script to `turbo.json` `build` inputs | ✅ — and ⭐ **the dev also added `$TURBO_ROOT$/scripts/invoked-as.mjs`**, the transitive dependency my message did not mention. A hash that covers the script but not what the script imports is still stale-able. |
| `package-files-exist` | the pinned exports list grew to four | ✅ with the three-things treatment written **into the test file**, quoting the 2026-08-17 ruling verbatim |

⭐ That pin comment does something better than what I asked for: it records **which direction is dangerous**. Growing is expected as further plugins adopt the step; *"shrinking it, by contrast, means a package stopped producing a sheet it still promises: that is objectui#4059's defect returning."* A pinned list that explains its own asymmetry will not be misread by the next person who has to move it.

⭐ The guard mechanism is also placed correctly: `isEntrypoint` sits in the **wrappers**, which are the entrypoints; the shared `scripts/build-plugin-stylesheet.mjs` has no guard because it is a library. My own check initially grepped the shared module and found nothing — the design is right, my probe was aimed one file over.

## The work itself

Both packages gain `src/index.css` in the `@reference` narrow shape (with the same header-comment discipline `fields` uses), a `scripts/build-css.mjs` step and the `"./style.css"` export. **16.30 kB and 11.41 kB** — against 172/164 kB for the unsubtracted compile, so the subtraction is doing real work. Build observed with both sheets **deleted first**, so emission is measured rather than assumed.

Re-measured on the merged tree by a **compiled-diff method rather than the card's literal grep**: 128 plugin-only classes absent from both published sheets, 25 themed — all 21 the card listed still hold, **plus 4 the grep method could not see**. No premise fork.

Degenerate control: `flex`, `text-sm`, `rounded-md`, `bg-background`, `sr-only` asserted **present** in the pre-subtraction compile and **absent** from the published sheet — so absence cannot be explained by the plugin never using the class.

Two unbuilt-worktree gate limitations (`check:doc-snippets`, `check:readme-exports`) named rather than glossed, with zero findings against the two touched packages. `content/docs/releases/` clean; changeset present.

⚠️ Filed by this run: **#6404** (`objectui run`'s temp app is only *partly* de-duplicable today — the other plugins still publish no sheet, so removing the restatement now would **move** the defect rather than fix it) and **#6405** (`fields`' build-css now duplicates the shared module). Both ungraded — triage's.
